captions.Figure 1: Held-out selective MAE effect under the frozen reliability policies. Selective MAE gain is defined as full-population MAE minus accepted-set MAE, so positive values indicate lower error among accepted predictions. FD001 is shown separately for its primary capped-RUL target and retained raw-RUL secondary analysis; FD002 uses the frozen piecewise-capped RUL target; FD003 uses uncapped RUL. FD004 is not represented as a performance bar because its primary held-out TEST evaluation was stopped before inference when 11 of 248 trajectories were shorter than the frozen 30-cycle input requirement. The figure does not imply comparability of absolute MAE across datasets.
captions.Figure 2: FD004 selective-gain direction across 381 executable controlled sensor-degradation scenarios. Positive selective gain occurred in 365 scenarios, zero gain in none, and negative gain in 16. All negative-gain cases belonged to the stuck-sensor family. These results are supporting DEV/corruption evidence and must not be interpreted as held-out TEST performance.
